sections.h2: Ways to sell a Southlake house
sections.html:
A Southlake seller can hire an agent, market the house privately or take a cash bid. Price range, the home's condition and your closing date drive the choice. The city sits at State Highway 114 and Farm Road 1709, seventeen miles north of Fort Worth, next to Grapevine, Keller and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. Most of the housing was built in the last four decades, which puts the age of your HVAC, roof and finishes squarely in a buyer's mind.

  • Agent: reaches the most buyers, but you stage, host showings and wait on the buyer's lender.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and take on the marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash bid: a quick as-is sale, priced to cover the buyer's repair costs and risk.

Judge each offer by what reaches you after the loan payoff, taxes and closing costs, since the headline price alone can mislead.

The city spans the Tarrant and Denton county line. Its tax page links to both the Tarrant County Appraisal District and the Denton County Appraisal District, and the side your house sits on decides its appraisal district, tax collector and county clerk.

Before you order a payoff or record a deed, read the county name on your tax bill or deed. Both documents, along with the legal description, name the county and the taxing units. Hand them to the title company on day one so it asks the right office for the payoff and uses the right clerk.

sections.h2: The city homestead exemption and tax pages
sections.html: Southlake offers a 20 percent homestead exemption and describes it as the highest state law allows. Texas now requires each city to post a notice that a parcel's estimated tax appears in the appraisal district's database, and Southlake does that with links to the Tarrant and Denton districts. The city also offers a form for property tax and budget questions. Search for your own parcel in the correct district's database instead of trusting a neighborhood average.

Statewide dates set what a seller owes at closing. January 1 is the key day: values and homestead qualification are fixed then, and the tax lien attaches.

Property tax dates that affect a Southlake sale
DateWhat happens
January 1Taxable value set, exemptions determined, tax lien attaches
April 1Notices of appraised value mailed for homesteads
May 15Last day to file most protests, or 30 days after the notice if later
October 1Tax bills mailed
November 30First half due under split payment
January 31Usual payment deadline
February 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
June 30Second half due under split payment

On top of the city's exemption, school districts give principal residences a $140,000 exemption, with $60,000 more for older or disabled owners.

sections.h2: If you think the value is too high
sections.html: Appraisal notices for homesteads go out around April 1. Most protests are due by May 15, or 30 days after the notice if that is later. File with the appraisal district for the county that holds your parcel, Tarrant or Denton, and gather what supports your case: repair estimates, photos and any recent sale prices nearby. Southlake's 20 percent homestead exemption and the school exemption both depend on your homestead filing, so make sure it is on record before you list. A buyer's agent will look at the same database page.

Southlake's Building Inspections division reviews plans, issues permits and performs inspections. Call (817) 748-8236 or stop by 1400 Main Street, Suite 250. Every contractor working in Southlake has to register, and general contractors renew annually. Registration is also required for trade contractors who hold a current state license.

Did you finish a basement, add a room or replace a roof or major system? Make sure each job was permitted and passed inspection. Inspectors and lenders working for a buyer may want proof, and a permit left open can hold up a closing. The permit system is online, so you can usually look up your address before you list. Inspection requests submitted by 7:00 a.m. are generally handled the same day.

If a past contractor never registered or closed a permit, clean that up before listing. It beats a surprise during a buyer's due diligence.

Southlake buyers often ask for paperwork early. Start with your payoff letter and the newest tax statement from the correct county. Next add the deed with its legal description and permit records for any remodel. Rented? Include the lease. Inherited? Include the will and any court papers. A cash buyer can move fast once these are in hand, and a listing agent will need most of them anyway. Having them ready also keeps you from learning about a missing permit or a lien the week before closing.

Southlake buyers compare houses closely. A listing that sits too long invites lower bids, and a house that needs work invites investors. Decide early which matters more to you, the highest price or a firm date. If a cash buyer offers a date you can plan around, weigh it against what an agent expects after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Ask every bidder in writing what happens if the title search finds a problem, and who pays for it. A clear answer now saves a dispute at the closing table.

Call City Hall at (817) 748-8400, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. A request portal called Southlake Serves handles questions that need follow-up. Residents use it to request a permit record, check a rule before listing or raise a concern about a neighbor's project that could affect a sale.

Depending on the parcel's location, either the Tarrant County Clerk or the Denton County Clerk records a Southlake deed. The signature needs an authorized officer's acknowledgment. Recording is priced per page with records charges added, so a longer document costs more, and your title company can give you the figure.

A will can be brought to probate by heirs for four years after the death. Where liens are the only debts, a muniment of title can move the property under the will. Estates worth more than $75,000, not counting the homestead and exempt property, are too large for a small estate affidavit.

If a mortgage is in default, the borrower has 20 days from the default notice to catch up. After 21 days' notice, an auction follows on a month's first Tuesday. A sale that closes first protects equity an auction might not.

The moment you say yes to a bid, the title company starts a file and hunts for liens, requesting tax figures from whichever county applies. A closing date is set, and you sign in front of a notary with photo ID, the deed and the latest tax bill. Since the parcel may be in Tarrant or Denton County, ask which clerk will record the deed. Proof of funds and the date should be on paper before you commit.

faqs.a: Both Tarrant and Denton counties. Your deed and tax bill show which one covers your parcel.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption does Southlake offer?
faqs.a: The city offers a 20 percent homestead exemption, which it calls the highest level state law allows. School districts add the state's $140,000 exemption.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Southlake property tax amount?
faqs.a: Look up your parcel in the Tarrant County or Denton County appraisal district database, which the city's tax page links to. Texas law requires that database to show estimated taxes.

faqs.q: Do I need permit proof to sell a Southlake house?
faqs.a: Not by law for every sale, but buyers and lenders often ask for it on remodels and additions. Southlake Building Inspections at (817) 748-8236 can tell you whether a permit was closed.

faqs.q: How soon can a Southlake house close for cash?
faqs.a: Often faster than a financed sale, since no loan approval is needed. Title work, liens, probate or a tenant can still set the pace, so ask each bidder for proof of funds and a written closing date.
